intro: Look up at the Halime Hatun Tomb, a tomb in Van province, built in 1358. This twelve-sided tomb tower rises above Lake Van at Gevaş. It is the best preserved piece of Kara Koyunlu stonework and, for its geometric carving, the emblem of the district.
history: The tomb was built in 1358 for Halime Hatun, daughter of the Kara Koyunlu lord Melik İzzeddin. It stands on a slope above Lake Van at Gevaş, in the middle of a cemetery of the same period. Walk slowly around it: the geometric and vegetal carving on its twelve faces follows a different arrangement on each one.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the twelve-sided shaft, the conical cap, the geometric carving and the cemetery that surrounds it.
facts: Did you know? The cemetery around the tomb holds hundreds of gravestones carved as rams and sheep — a form particular to eastern Anatolia, carried over from nomadic practice. And on the tomb itself, each of the twelve faces carries a different arrangement of carving; not one is repeated.
outro: This brings our tour of the Halime Hatun Tomb to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. May the quiet of this place stay with you a little longer. Enjoy your visit.
